question: Does a minimal four-edge extension of the ideal D4 three-edge chain make a genuinely new or changed second-site charge record first-dependent, and does nonbranching versus a three-arm branch alter that answer?
epistemic_role: Small exact physical-topology falsification matrix on one fixed L=2 vacuum orbit; not a general transition kernel, noisy history, decoder or schedule-risk study
source_basis: Jing et al. 2025 Appendix A.2/A.4: red-X error strings, flux-free quasi-stabilizer readout, ordered post-flux correction measurements and chain/branch distinctions
J6L periodic incidence, J6M compact common vacuum orbit and J6Q ordered Born projector law
J6R/J6S/J6T three-edge exact public-law and repeated-versus-new-site controls

physical_and_observation_contract.geometry: J6L periodic L=2, 24 blue/green sites, 108 kagome qubits and J6M common +1 star/triangle orbit from |0^108>
physical_and_observation_contract.incidence: Path [0,4,3,7] runs blue:0-green:1-blue:2-green:3-blue:4 with no repeated vertices. Branch [0,4,3,5] has degree three at blue:2, degree two at green:1, and three distinct leaf vertices; neither contains a cycle.
physical_and_observation_contract.causal_order: Prepare same J6M orbit; apply private red-X edges; jointly project all first flux-free stars; apply a specified public red-X correction; jointly project all residual-flux-free second stars in the actual first-postselected sector.
physical_and_observation_contract.public_record: Only full 24-bit flux/charge/vacuum arrays with zero charge at fluxful unmeasured sites; no private error support, operator identity, site-partition or truth in public arrays.
physical_and_observation_contract.noise: Ideal exact Born projector law only; no readout noise or stochastic physical histories

competing_outcomes: A novel second-site joint charge law differs across positive first public records for at least one path/action; report whether dependence occurs at a newly eligible site or only at a changed operator.
A novel-site effect occurs only on one of the two topologies, distinguishing path from branch in this finite ideal fixture.
All complete branches are novel-site independent and any full-record effect is unchanged-observable repetition; the four-edge matrix does not witness transfer.
One or more branches exceed the registered support/compute cap; retain only censored diagnostics for those branches and make no complete-law claim there.

action_edge_lists.matched_all_four: same four physical edges in listed order

matrix.independent_unit: One fixed exact initial state per geometry with four counterfactual correction actions, not Monte Carlo samples
matrix.analysis: At fixed geometry/action compare full conditional second public distributions across every positive first public record, then exact projections onto newly eligible sites and onto newly eligible plus changed-operator sites. List positive joint support and probability; never infer independence from only site marginals.

acceptance: All eight source/prior/caller hashes, exact J6L path versus branch incidence and unchanged five-round caller pass.

For each of eight geometry/action branches, eligible sites equal flux-free sites; eligible stars commute in the actual triangle sector, and exact first/conditional second rational masses are nonnegative and normalized or the branch is explicitly censored at the registered site cap.
Every complete positive row contains only first and second full 24-bit public flux/charge/vacuum arrays plus exact probabilities; site partitions and physical support remain private diagnostics.

Report complete-law dependence on full public records separately from new-only and changed-plus-new joint projections, with path/branch contrast, censored branches and no post-hoc action substitution.
Zero histories, schedule-arm evaluations, bootstraps, decoder comparison, threshold fits or five-round caller changes; no promotion beyond this one ideal L=2 orbit.
stop_rule: Fail closed on provenance/incidence drift, noncommuting eligible projectors, negative/unnormalized mass, public/private leakage, caller mutation or total CPU overrun. If more than four first or six second sites are nondeterministic, censor only that geometry/action branch without raising the bound or choosing replacement geometry.
